title: Relative clauses 1
note: who/which/that + where/when/why · defining · omission page. · Bank 64 · full-pronoun expansion + that-rebalance 2026-07-27 · RUE2 TRANSPLANT 2026-08-25: blocks+intro restored from rue2-grok-v1.0 (James-smoked, quality=good_draft); auto-authored bank superseded. · 2026-08-28 smoke: intro 6 cards; Quiz chips who/which/that/what (how after the way); Type = same gap; Use = join two sentences. · 2026-09-04 B1 loop: B3 all 66 gap items had no authored chips — each now offers the answer plus three relatives that are wrong for THIS head, never a form its own gap_accepts also accepts (that and which are both right on a thing head, so neither can be a distractor there); *what* is on the chips because it is the Czech co error the mistakes card already names. D1 four explanations covered all 66; each now says whether the head is a person, a thing, a place, a time or a reason, and which relative that rules out. A8 thirteen twins closed. C4 three bolded fragments now bold the taught word only (C13). C23 'in this pack' off the place/time/reason card.

items.en: The man who called is my boss.

accepts: The man who called is my boss.

cards.title: What they are

rows: The man called. ~~He~~ is my boss.
The man **who called** is my boss.
The book is useful. I bought ~~it~~.
The book **which** I bought is useful.

points: They are attached to a noun
They say which person or which thing you mean
They come immediately after that noun

cards.title: who / which / that
points: who = people · which = things · that = both
který is people and things. English splits them.

cards.title: Two patterns

rows: The man **who called** is my boss.
The book **which** I bought is useful.

points: Look at the word after who / which / that
A verb comes next → the noun does the action
I / you / we comes next → someone else does it

cards.title: Leave it out

rows: The man **who** called is my boss.
The book **which** I bought is useful.
The book I bought is useful.

points: Drop it only when a new subject follows
Never drop it when a verb follows
Never keep the old object: bought it ✗

cards.title: Place, time, reason
points: Do not add at or in after where

cards.title: Typical mistakes
points: After a noun, Czech co is that / which, not what
který splits: who for people, which for things
